ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Meconium aspiration: 1

A post-term newborn develops respiratory distress after delivery through thick meconium-stained fluid. Imaging shows patchy lung opacities with areas of hyperinflation. Which syndrome best unifies the exposure and respiratory findings while other neonatal causes are evaluated?

  1. Partial airway obstruction with air trapping
  2. Chemical pneumonitis with surfactant dysfunction
  3. Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
  4. Prioritize effective ventilation; suction only when obstruction warrants it
  5. Meconium aspiration syndrome
Answer and explanation

Meconium aspiration syndrome

Respiratory distress after meconium exposure in a term or post-term infant can reflect aspiration-related lung disease; other causes still require consideration.

Option explanations

Meconium aspiration syndrome: Respiratory distress after meconium exposure in a term or post-term infant can reflect aspiration-related lung disease; other causes still require consideration.

Partial airway obstruction with air trapping: A ball-valve effect permits inspiration more readily than expiration, promoting hyperinflation and air leak. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Chemical pneumonitis with surfactant dysfunction: Meconium injures the lung and disrupts surfactant, contributing to impaired gas exchange and atelectasis. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn: Persistently high pulmonary vascular resistance can drive right-to-left shunting and worsen hypoxemia in severe neonatal lung disease. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Prioritize effective ventilation; suction only when obstruction warrants it: Routine suction solely for meconium exposure can delay needed ventilation. Obstruction preventing effective ventilation may require airway clearance. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
